purpose: Teduglutide is used to treat adults and children with short bowel syndrome, a condition where part of the small intestine is missing or has been removed. Because of this, the body has trouble absorbing enough nutrients and fluids from food. This medication helps reduce how much intravenous (IV) nutrition a person needs each day.
how_it_works: Your small intestine has a lining that absorbs nutrients and fluids. Teduglutide works like a natural hormone in your body called GLP-2, which helps that lining grow thicker and healthier. A healthier intestinal lining means your gut can absorb more nutrients and fluids on its own, so you may need less IV nutrition over time.
common_side_effects: Stomach pain or cramping, nausea, vomiting, bloating or gas, swelling of the hands or feet (fluid retention), reactions at the injection site (redness, swelling, or pain), and headache are among the most commonly reported side effects.
warnings: Teduglutide can cause abnormal growths (polyps) in the intestine or colon, so your doctor will require regular colonoscopies before and during treatment. It may also cause blockages in the bowel or gallbladder problems. Tell your doctor right away if you have severe stomach pain, yellowing of the skin or eyes, or sudden changes in your bowel habits. People with a history of cancer, especially intestinal or colorectal cancer, should discuss risks carefully with their doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 0.05 mg per kilogram of your body weight, injected under the skin once daily. Your healthcare team will calculate the exact dose for you and teach you how to give the injection at home, usually in the thigh, abdomen, or upper arm. It is important to inject it at the same time each day.
